name: Quillon Prime Ladder Problem
summary: Made-up sample problem. A Quillon ladder is a fictional kind of infinite sequence of primes in which each prime limits where the next one can fall. The problem asked how many ladders it takes for every infinite set of primes to share infinitely many members with at least one of them: as many as there are real numbers, or fewer? In 2025 the question was shown to be independent of the standard axioms of set theory, so it can be neither proved nor disproved from them.

progress.title: Ladders defined and the question posed
progress.description: The rule linking each prime in a ladder to the next was fixed, and the counting question was stated in its current form. All ladders taken together are always enough, so the question is whether fewer will do.

progress.title: Countably many ladders are never enough
progress.description: A diagonal argument showed that no countable family of ladders is enough: some infinite set of primes always shares only finitely many members with each ladder. So in any model of set theory with no infinite size between that of the whole numbers and that of the real numbers, as many ladders as real numbers are needed. Such models exist, so the axioms cannot rule that answer out.

links.title: Write-up of the diagonal argument (sample link)

progress.title: Prime-gap proof attempts
progress.description: Several attempts tried to settle the question using only facts about the gaps between primes. Such facts handle only countably many ladders at a time, so they cannot decide it. The later independence result confirms that this route cannot work.

links.title: Notes on the failed attempts (sample link)

progress.title: Question shown independent of the standard axioms
progress.description: A model of set theory was built in which fewer ladders than there are real numbers are enough. With the 2016 result, this means the standard axioms can neither prove nor disprove that as many ladders as real numbers are needed. That closes the problem as posed. An AI model first suggested the key counting step, which was then proved by hand.

links.title: AI session log for the counting step (sample link)

progress.title: Machine-checked proof of both halves
progress.description: Formalize both halves of the independence result in a proof assistant, so it does not rest on a hand check. The countable bound is done; the model construction is about half finished.

progress.title: Check which extra axioms decide the question
progress.description: Find out whether widely studied extra axioms of set theory settle the question one way or the other. This is a follow-up: it would not reopen the problem as posed.
